column5: Look: modern 16-bit pixel *(provisional)*. Mood: a warm surface by day and a cold blue night. Scale: 16-pixel tiles at whole-number scale, with a camera that never moves in sub-pixels. Shapes: blocky world, a small rounded digger, sharp angular monsters. Palette: earth browns and moss green for the ground, cool grey stone, the player in warm orange, threats in sickly violet with bright eyes, ore as the glinting accent; shadows cooler, lights warmer. Rules: one pixel density, a dark one-pixel outline on figures only, flat shading with one highlight step. Signature: darkness that swallows the caves, with torchlight carving warm pools out of it. Every figure drawn, no emoji, no plain circles.
References: Terraria (the side-view dig, build and night loop; not its art, names or characters).
View: 2D · Camera: side view that follows the digger.
A side-view world generated from a seed each run: surface, dirt, stone, caves, ore, trees
Digging that cracks blocks in steps, with harder rock deeper and rock that says what tool it needs
Ore that glints before you reach it, and pickups that fly to you
A craft list that shows what you can make now and what greyed recipes are missing
Block placing on a grid with a ghost preview, for walls, doors and torches
A day and night cycle with felt dusk, darkness and torchlight
3 night monster kinds, each attacking differently (a walker that chews walls, a leaper, a flyer)

You stand on grass under a low sun with a pickaxe in hand.
Holding the mouse on dirt cracks it in steps and the bits fly to you.
A tree gives wood and the crafting list lights up with a torch and wood walls, while greyed recipes say what they still need.
An ore glint a few tiles down pulls you into the first cave, where it gets dark until you place a torch.
Then the sky starts to turn.
You climb out and wall yourself in as the first monster reaches the door.
*(guessed)*
The first night comes about two minutes in.
A basic walled shelter with a torch survives it.
Monsters walk at you and chew through weak walls, so dirt holds briefly and stone holds longer.
Dying drops what you carried where you fell and you wake at your bed.
Each night brings more monsters and a new kind.
*(provisional)*
